title: Digits Adding to Forty-Seven
statement: What is the smallest positive integer that is a multiple of $11$ and whose digits add up to $47$?
hints: Split the digits into two groups: those in the $1$st, $3$rd, $5$th, $\dots$ places counting from the right, and those in the $2$nd, $4$th, $6$th, $\dots$ places. Let $x$ and $y$ be the sums of the two groups.
A number is a multiple of $11$ exactly when $x - y$ is. Here $x + y = 47$ is odd, so $x - y$ is odd as well, and in particular it cannot be $0$.

So $x - y$ is $\pm 11$ or $\pm 33$, and one of $x$ and $y$ is at least $29$. That group needs at least $4$ digits, so the number has at least $7$. With exactly $7$ digits, find $x$ and $y$, then make the digits as small as possible from the left.
solution:
Let $x$ and $y$ be the sums of the digits in the odd and the even places, counting from the right. The number is a multiple of $11$ exactly when $11$ divides $x - y$. As $x + y = 47$ is odd, $x - y$ is odd too, hence $\pm 11$ or $\pm 33$, and one of $x$, $y$ is at least $\frac{47 + 11}{2} = 29$. Three digits add up to at most $27$, so that group has at least $4$ digits and the number has at least $7$.

With $7$ digits the odd places hold $4$ digits and the even places $3$, so $x \le 36$ and $y \le 27$, which leaves only $x = 29$ and $y = 18$. The three odd-place digits after the first add up to at most $27$, so the first digit is at least $2$. If it is $2$, the other odd-place digits are all $9$, and the even-place digits, adding up to $18$, are smallest as $0$, $9$, $9$ from the left. The answer is $2099999 = 11 \cdot 190909$.
